# Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street

## Problem Statement

Main Street is single-player only; the `MainStreetState`, `MainStreetEngine`, and PRD M3 were never designed for an opponent. Players asked for competitive play — racing an AI on the shared street grid — but the engine assumes single ownership of coins, hand, actions, street slots, and score. Adding competitive mode requires splitting those concerns while preserving single-player behaviour and the existing AI/hint/Monte Carlo stack.

## Users & User Stories

- **Player (competitive mode):** As a Main Street player, I want to play against an AI opponent on the same shared street so each turn I have a rival to race and react to.
- **Developer / QA:** As a developer, I want a head-to-head Monte Carlo harness for competitive mode so balance between player and AI can be measured across seeded runs.
- **Future AI iteration:** As an AI developer, I want the AI decision layer ownership-aware and staff-free so competitive strategy is coherent without rewriting the hint/balance harness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Per-player state & ownership:** A competitive state model exists with per-player coins/reputation, hand, staff, action budget, and score, plus owner-tagged street slots; deterministic and replayable via seeded RNG. Single-player behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC2 — AI plays a legal competitive turn:** The AI generates legal actions through `enumerateLegalActions` (competitive mode) with staff actions excluded, scored by an ownership-aware `scoreAction`/helpers, and executed via `executeAction`. Verified with legality and determinism tests.
- [ ] **AC3 — Per-owner income; shared events:** Income accrues only to the owning player of each placed business; street-wide investment events and incidents retain their existing resolution semantics, routed per-owner as specified. Validated by income/event unit tests.
- [ ] **AC4 — Competitive Monte Carlo harness:** A head-to-head harness (extending `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) runs >=200 seeds and produces win/score distributions plus per-player metrics; single-player AI tests still pass.
- [ ] **AC5 — Engine-only scope confirmed:** PRD M3 is updated to note this deliberate scope extension; competitive mode has no game-selector entry or scene yet — rendering (owner-coloured street, shared-market phase alternation with SFX/animations per AGENTS.md 8) is deferred to a planning-created child.
- [ ] **AC6 — Tests & docs:** Relevant unit tests and new tests cover AC1–AC4; build succeeds; affected docs/comments are updated.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full test suite passes** with the new changes (release gate; not a per-push requirement beyond `npm run build` + unit tests).

## Constraints

- Competitive mode scope is **state + engine + AI + Monte Carlo only** — no game selector entry, no competitive scene, no competitive UI chrome yet (AC5 deferred to a planning child).
- Turn alternation: **alternate MarketPhases within a shared day** (confirmed producer decision). Income/Incident/EndCheck phases are shared once both players have acted. Implementation design stays within planning.
- Win condition: **first player to reach the win threshold wins**; the game offers an endless continuation option beyond threshold (confirmed producer decision). Endless mode wiring is within the parent unless planning creates a dedicated child.
- `MainStreetAiPlayer` / `MainStreetAiStrategy` / `GreedyStrategy` / `scoreAction` / `enumerateLegalActions` are unchanged for single-player consumers.
- Determinism via seeded RNG is preserved; replays remain reproducible.

## Existing State

- Single-player-only state (`MainStreetState` resourceBank/hand/staffCards/actionsRemaining), engine (`applyIncome`, `resolveEvent`, `resolveIncident`, `computeScore`, `checkEndConditions`), PRD M3, and AI layers (`MainStreetAiStrategy`, `GreedyStrategy`, `scoreAction`, `MainStreetAiPlayer`, `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) built for one owner. Reusability findings documented in the original description.
- One child item already exists: **CG-0MT5X3N79002S038 — Competitive AI strategy (ownership-aware, staff-free)**.

## Desired Change

Ship an **engine-level competitive mode**: per-player state + owner-tagged grid, per-owner income routing, shared event semantics, ownership-aware and staff-free AI scoring, and a competitive Monte Carlo harness — without changing single-player behaviour or adding competitive rendering. Record the scope extension in PRD M3 and plan the rendering/scene child for the next milestone.

## Decisions Since Original Item

- **Turn structure:** Option A (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day) confirmed by producer.
- **AC5:** Deferred to planning — will become a child for rendering/selector/scene work.
- **Denial reasoning:** Opponent-aware denial (blocking best slot, buying to deny) intentionally deferred to a follow-up child.
- **Win condition:** First to threshold wins, with an endless continuation option beyond threshold.
- **Owner-coloured street (AC5):** Means tinting each placed business's street slot by owner (e.g., player = blue, AI = red) so the shared grid's ownership is visually unambiguous.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Split to per-player resources/hand/staff/actions/score; owner-tagged `StreetGrid` slots.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Per-owner income, shared event/incident routing, shared-day phase handling, competitive helpers.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Ownership-aware `scoreAction`/per-type helpers + competitive `enumerateLegalActions` variant (staff excluded); single-player paths unchanged.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Competitive head-to-head harness (extension).
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md` — Note competitive mode as deliberate scope extension beyond M3.
- `tests/main-street/*.test.ts` (+ new competitive tests) — Unit + deterministic replay coverage for AC1–AC4; existing guardrails still passing.

## Related Work

- Related work items (from `find_related`): CG-0MM5ZGB8U02S0BFO — Main Street Scenario & Tutorial (completed) · CG-0MOXGGZXJ002X6H3 — [test-failure] MainStreetScene animation scheduling (completed) · CG-0MS9NXIEX00880UV — [test-failure] hud-layer-contract (completed)
- Related docs (from repo scan): `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md` · `docs/DEVELOPER.md` · `AGENTS.md`
- Child: CG-0MT5X3N79002S038 — Competitive AI strategy (existing; align description with this parent's clarified ACs).
- Existing state/engine/AI/monte-carlo layers are the implementation basis (see Existing State above).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **State split regressions in single player:** score/income/event paths silently ignore per-player split. Mitigation: keep single-player API shim and run full single-player regression suite.
- **Income/event routing divergence:** per-owner bugs hard to diagnose. Mitigation: explicit per-owner unit fixtures + deterministic replay across seeds.
- **AI ownership semantics under-tested:** greedy heuristics mis-score denial/synergy when ownership added. Mitigation: head-to-head harness + baseline comparisons (AC4).
- **Phase alternation complexity:** alternating MarketPhases within one day adds state machine edge cases. Mitigation: diagram shared-day phases in planning and cover transitions with unit tests.
- **Scope creep toward rendering:** temptation to start the selector/scene early. Mitigation: AC5 is explicitly deferred; new rendering asks become planning-linked children.

## Open Questions

None — all open intake questions have been answered by the producer (see Comments). Remaining design detail (per-player state shape, phase machine, Monte Carlo metrics schema, endless-mode trigger) is within planning.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Alternating turn structure — Option A (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day) vs Option B (alternate full days)?" — Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "a" → resolved as **Option A** (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day). Recorded in `wl comment` (producer decisions comment).
- Q2 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Child item coverage for AC5 — create competitive-scene child now or defer to planning?" — Answer (producer): "planning. for now what do you mean by 'owner colored streets'" → resolved as **deferred to planning**; follow-up clarification Q5 added. Recorded in `wl comment`.
- Q3 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Denial reasoning scope — deferred or minimum viable?" — Answer (producer): "deferred" → denial is **out of scope** for this epic, may become a follow-up child.
- Q4 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Win condition — first to threshold, fixed days, or simultaneous?" — Answer (producer): "when one player rea hes a win conditiion with option to carry on in endless mode" → **first to threshold wins, with endless continuation option**.
- Q5 (Map, implicit follow-up): "What does 'owner coloured streets' mean?" — Answer purpose: rendering the shared street grid where each placed business slot is visually tinted by owner (e.g., player blue, AI red) so ownership is immediately readable. Scene concern deferred to planning child.

## Goal (user story)

As a developer, I want a shared-day phase machine where MarketPhases alternate within a day (Option A) and Income/Incident/EndCheck resolve once both players have acted, so competitive turns interleave tightly before shared resolution.

## Context

DayPhase is single-player (DayStart → MarketPhase → InvestmentResolution → IncomePhase → IncidentPhase → EndCheck). No concept of “whose turn within the day” exists. Expected shared-day flow (Option A, confirmed): both players alternate MarketPhases, then shared closing phases run once. This child depends on the competitive state model's active-player tracking.

## Scope

- Shared-day phase machine: active-player index, alternating MarketPhases, then shared Income/Incident/EndCheck.
- Win condition: first player to reach the win threshold wins (confirmed decision).
- Single-player (N=1) unchanged: same sequence with one MarketPhase.
- Diagram shared-day phases in code comment + cover transitions with unit tests.

## Out of scope

- Per-owner income/event routing (sibling — this child's closing phases delegate to that sibling).
- AI strategy / Monte Carlo.
- Endless continuation (deferred to separate top-level issue).
- Rendering / scene (AC5 child).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** Shared-day phase machine alternates MarketPhases within a day across N players (active-player tracking), then shared Income/Incident/EndCheck resolve once all players have acted; sequence verified by unit tests including edge cases (action budget hand-off, phase entry/exit invariants).
- [ ] **AC2:** Win condition is first-to-threshold (first player to reach win threshold wins); EndCheck detects the winner correctly.
- [ ] **AC3:** N=1 (single player) preserves the legacy phase sequence with one MarketPhase per day.
- [ ] **AC4:** Phase diagram documented in code comment; transitions covered by unit tests.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Shared-day phase machine (`processEndOfTurn` / phase handlers, first-to-threshold check).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Phase types, active-player index.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-phase.test.ts` — Dedicated competitive phase tests (alternation, shared closing, win condition, N=1 regression).

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30
- Depends on: competitive state model (per-player active-player + threshold)
- Delegates to: per-owner income/event routing sibling for Income/Incident semantics
- Architecture: N-player-ready (sequence iterates PlayerRecord[]; N is not hardcoded to 2)

# Intake Brief: Add a dev mode cheat to add a specific card to the market (CG-0MTINKHUT009KHK5)

**Priority: Critical** | **Type: Feature** | **Assignee: Map**

> Add a dev-mode debug tool that lets a tester replace a random current market card with any card in the Main Street pool. Entry is a button in the Settings panel Debug Tools section (visible only under `import.meta.env.DEV` via the existing `DebugToolsEntry`/`CardGameScene` debug-tools framework). Selecting a card via mouse or keyboard (arrow keys + Enter) performs the replacement and refreshes the market display.

## Problem Statement

Debugging Main Street gameplay that depends on specific market cards (business, community space, event, upgrade, or staff) is slow without a way to force a desired card into the 3-card single-row market. A dev-mode cheat that replaces a random market card with a chosen card will make it possible to reproduce and validate edge cases (progression gating, deck composition, economy constraints, synergy adjacency, and staff-skill assignment) on demand without manipulating saves or seeds.

## Users

- **Engine / game developer debugging Main Street:** Needs to force a specific business, community-space, event, upgrade, or staff card into the market to reproduce layout, synergy, or gating bugs.
  - *"As a developer, I want to open a card picker from the Debug Tools section and inject a chosen card into the market so I can reproduce a synergy or tier-gating scenario in one click."*
- **QA / manual tester validating progression and balance:** Needs to exercise rare or tier-gated cards without grinding through many refreshes or seeded deals.
  - *"As a QA tester, I want to search the full card pool by name and add a specific card to the market so I can verify its interactions without waiting for it to appear naturally."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Dev-mode gated Debug Tools entry:** A button/entry appears in the Settings panel Debug Tools section only when running under `npm run dev` (`import.meta.env.DEV === true` via the existing `isDevMode()` / `SettingsPanel` `debugTools` / `CardGameScene.initSettingsPanel` framework). In production builds the entry and its code are absent / tree-shaken and the production bundle does not expose the feature.

2. **Card picker window on activation:** Clicking the debug entry opens a window/panel that lists **all cards in the game** (all Main Street card families — Business, Community Space, Event, Upgrade, Staff) derived from the live card template registry (`getBusinessTemplates()`, `getCommunitySpaceTemplates()`, `getEventTemplates()`, `getUpgradeTemplates()`, `getStaffCardTemplates()` / `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES` in `MainStreetCards.ts`), respecting the currently loaded CSV (`getCsvRows()` / `loadTemplatesFromCsv` reload path).

3. **Grouped + filtered presentation:** The picker groups cards by type/family and provides at least (a) a type filter (select one or more families) and (b) a text box that filters by partial title match (case-insensitive substring against the card display name). Filters compose (type ∩ text); clearing filters shows the full grouped list again.

4. **Mouse and keyboard selection:** A card can be selected by mouse click **or** by keyboard (arrow keys to move focus/selection, Enter to confirm). The picker is operable without a mouse.

5. **Replace a random market card:** Confirming a selection replaces a **random** card among the **currently available market cards** (`state.market.cards`, length `MARKET_TOTAL_SLOTS === 3` in `MainStreetCards.ts` / `MainStreetState.ts`) with the chosen card. The random choice is uniformly over the current market slots; the market row is re-rendered immediately and the game state remains valid (no duplicate-id corruption — the injected card receives a distinct instance `id`; if the source template holds multiple copies, one fresh instance is created). The displaced card is returned to its family's discard/deck per the existing Main Street market lifecycle (do not lose cards).

6. **Non-destructive and reversible via existing flows:** The replacement does not corrupt save/load (versioned serialization), transcript recording, undo/redo, or tutorial scenario state; subsequent market refreshes/cycling continue to use the normal deck/discard pipelines. If a nicer UX is needed, the operation may be wired as a command so undo returns the market to its prior composition (nice-to-have, not required).

7. **Testing and gating validation:**
   - Unit tests cover: dev-mode gating of the tool, picker filtering/grouping logic, keyboard navigation, and the market-replacement effect (random slot replacement, deck/discard handling, valid-state invariants).
   - At least one targeted browser test verifies the panel opens from the Settings debug section and a card can be chosen by mouse.
   - `npm run build` succeeds and the production bundle does not contain the debug card-picker code.

8. **Documentation update:** Docs that describe debug tools / Main Street development workflows are updated to mention the new cheat (e.g. `docs/DEVELOPER.md` or the Main Street dev section).

9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

10. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing dev-mode debug framework: `isDevMode()` / `DebugToolsRegistry.DebugToolsEntry` (`src/ui/debug/DebugToolsRegistry.ts`), `SettingsPanel` `debugTools` rendering, and `CardGameScene.initSettingsPanel` default debug-tools wiring — follow the pattern of `SessionExportTool`, `StateInspectorOverlay`, `GameEventLogOverlay`, `AiDecisionOverlay`. Gate the tool via `import.meta.env.DEV` so it is tree-shaken from production bundles.
- **Absolute no-no:** No debug/release transition bugs — the feature must be completely absent in production (no UI, no reachable code path, no bundle bloat). No arbitrary code execution or file-system access from the picker.
- Market model is single-row, exactly `MARKET_TOTAL_SLOTS` (3) cards (`MainStreetCards.ts`); replacement targets `state.market.cards` (Main Street state) and must go through the existing renderer (`MainStreetRenderer`) and animation/layout paths rather than bypassing them.
- Card pool is the CSV-backed template registry (`MainStreetCards.ts` `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES` / `get*Templates()` / `getCsvRows()`); the picker must handle runtime CSV reload (`loadTemplatesFromCsv`) and tier-gated pools (unlocked-card filtering) without duplicating template data inline.

## Existing State

- `MainStreetCards.ts` defines all five families, CSV-backed templates (`getBusinessTemplates()` etc.), `MARKET_TOTAL_SLOTS = 3`, and `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES`; `MainStreetEngine.ts` / `MainStreetState.ts` own `state.market.cards` and market lifecycle (refill/cycle/refresh).
- Dev-mode Debug Tools framework exists (`src/ui/debug/`, `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts`, `src/ui/CardGameScene.ts`) with `isDevMode()`, `DebugToolsEntry`, and default tools (`SessionExport`, `StateInspector`, `GameEventLog`, `AiDecisionViewer`); production gating via `import.meta.env.DEV` is established.
- No existing mechanism forces an arbitrary card into the market — market contents are derived from the seeded deck + cycling; reproducing specific-card scenarios requires seed manipulation or save hacking.

## Desired Change

- Register a new `DebugToolsEntry` (e.g. `createMarketCardCheatTool`) that opens a card picker overlay/window: grouped by family/type, with a type filter and a partial-title text filter, navigable by mouse and keyboard (arrow keys + Enter).
- On confirm, replace a uniformly-random entry of `state.market.cards` with a freshly-instantiated card from the chosen template (unique instance `id`), return the displaced card to its family discard/deck per existing lifecycle, and re-render the market row (reuse `MainStreetRenderer` / `MainStreetScene` refresh path). Ensure save/load, undo/redo, and transcript invariants remain intact.
- Wire the tool into the default debug-tools set (or Main-Street-specific override of `CardGameScene.initSettingsPanel`) and document it.

## Key Files

- `src/ui/debug/DebugToolsRegistry.ts` — `isDevMode()` + `DebugToolsEntry` interface; extended with the new entry factory.
- `src/ui/debug/index.ts` — Barrel re-export; add the new tool factory.
- `src/ui/CardGameScene.ts` — `initSettingsPanel` default `debugTools` wiring; register the new tool (globally or via Main Street scene override).
- `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` — Debug Tools section rendering (consumes `debugTools`); no structural change expected, but verify scroll/selection interaction.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — Card pool source of truth: `MARKET_TOTAL_SLOTS`, `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES`, `getBusinessTemplates()` / `getCommunitySpaceTemplates()` / `getEventTemplates()` / `getUpgradeTemplates()` / `getStaffCardTemplates()`, `getCsvRows()` / `loadTemplatesFromCsv` / tier helpers; add any small helpers for "instantiate a fresh card from a template id" if not already centralized.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — `state.market.cards` shape and deck/discard families (move displaced card to correct pile).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Market lifecycle (refill/cycle/discard routing) — where to slot the cheat's state mutation so it obeys the same invariants.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — Scene wiring: renderer ownership, debug-tools override, overlay dismissal, keyboard focus management for the picker.
- `src/ui/debug/MarketCardCheatOverlay.ts` (new) — Overlay/window implementation: grouped list, type filter, title substring filter, arrow-key + Enter + mouse selection, confirm → engine call, cancel/dismiss.

## Related Work

- **Potentially related docs:**
  - `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Developer workflow, testing, and Main Street local development; will need a note about the new debug cheat.
  - `src/ui/debug/DebugToolsRegistry.ts`, `src/ui/debug/StateInspectorOverlay.ts`, `src/ui/debug/GameEventLogOverlay.ts`, `src/ui/debug/AiDecisionOverlay.ts` — Canonical patterns for overlay-based debug tools registered as `DebugToolsEntry`.
- **Potentially related work items:**
  - Detect when running in developer mode and provide debug tools (CG-0MQZYFG3C0063DN3) — Epic that created the Debug Tools framework; this item extends it.
  - Dev mode detection & Debug section framework (CG-0MS217X1F0089SAM) — Created `isDevMode()` / `SettingsPanel` debug section.
  - Session export in Debug section (CG-0MS1QC3RR004J4Y5), Game Event Log debug tool (CG-0MS1QC3KR004C7UQ), and siblings — Prior art for adding entries to the debug section.
  - Minimal Card System & Market (CG-0MM7IA8UB0BOEXZ5), Single-row market UI & input flows (CG-0MSW6ITE50095JJ4), MarketOfferEngine Extraction (CG-0MPWZ5RYR005VX1F) — Market implementation history.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** The card pool is exactly the runtime template registry in `MainStreetCards.ts` (CSV-backed, `get*Templates()`); if the pool is expected to include only unlocked/tier-available cards, the picker should consult the current unlock state rather than the full catalog — confirm desired scope during implementation.
- **Risk — debug code leaks into production:** Mitigate by gating factory creation/import behind `import.meta.env.DEV` in `CardGameScene.initSettingsPanel` and verifying the production bundle does not contain picker code (bundle inspection / smoke test).
- **Risk — state corruption (duplicate ids, discard/deck inconsistency):** Mitigate by instantiating the replacement via a dedicated helper that clones the template with a unique instance `id` (e.g. `${templateId}--cheat-${nonce}`) and by routing the displaced card through the existing discard path per family.
- **Risk — accessibility / focus management:** Arrow-key + Enter navigation and focus trapping inside the overlay must work alongside `SettingsPanel` and existing HUD overlays — follow patterns in `StateInspectorOverlay` / `GameEventLogOverlay` for scroll, mask, and dismiss handling.
- **Risk — scope creep (deck editors, multi-card injection, staff-skill reseed):** Treat richer cheats (add-to-deck, reseed skills, inject multiple cards) as follow-up work items rather than extending this item — this item replaces a single random market card only.
- **Scope-creep guard:** Extra cheat concepts surfaced during planning (e.g. deck/discard editors, tier override, skill reseed) should be filed as separate `discovered-from:CG-0MTINKHUT009KHK5` work items.

## Effort & Risk (to be filled by /skill:effort-and-risk)

*Filled by `orchestrate_estimate.py` after intake.*

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- **Q1:** Which cards should appear in the picker — the full Main Street pool across all five families as defined by `MainStreetCards.ts` / `card-data.csv`, or a filtered subset (e.g. only currently unlocked / tier-available cards)? *(No user answer yet — inferred as full pool; confirm during planning.)* — **Status: OPEN QUESTION** — No direct input from the work-item description; using the full template registry is the safest default. If the intended behavior is "only currently available" cards (respecting progression tiers), the picker should consult the game's unlock state instead. Flag for producer confirmation.
- **Q2:** Should the replacement be undoable via the existing undo/redo command stack, or is a simple state mutation acceptable for this dev-only cheat? *(No user answer — inferred as non-undoable, with undo as an optional nice-to-have.)* — **Status: OPEN QUESTION** — The description does not mention undo. A simple mutation is acceptable; wiring as a command is a polish item. Flag for producer preference before implementation.
- **Q3:** Is the project-scoped or Main-Street-specific placement preferred for the new tool? The description is Main-Street-specific ("all the cards in the game" + "replace a card in the market" — Main Street has a market; other example games do not), so a Main-Street scene override of `debugTools` is assumed rather than a global default. Confirm if the tool should appear in every game scene's debug section. — **Status: OPEN QUESTION** — No direct input; description scope suggests Main Street only. Implementation note records the assumption so it can be corrected before plan/implement.

*Research performed for this intake (no producer interview required — work item was sufficiently detailed to draft the brief without blocking):*

- Searched Worklog (`wl search market`, `wl search dev mode`) and the repository for the existing Debug Tools framework (`src/ui/debug/`, `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts`, `src/ui/CardGameScene.ts`) and Main Street's card/market model (`example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts`, `MainStreetState.ts`, `MainStreetEngine.ts`, `MainStreetScene.ts`) to confirm the single-row 3-card market, the CSV-backed `get*Templates()` / `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES` pool, and the `import.meta.env.DEV`-gated `DebugToolsEntry` pattern. No blocking clarifications were required to produce a testable acceptance-criteria set; open questions above capture scope ambiguities that can be resolved at plan time without holding up intake.

Completed work pushed to dev, see commit 36ac9108.

Shared-day phase machine (Option A): DayStart → N alternating MarketPhases (activePlayerId round-robin) → shared InvestmentResolution/IncomePhase/IncidentPhase → EndCheck (first-to-threshold, lowest index wins) → DayStart(next). N=1 collapses to legacy single-player path.

Engine: getActivePlayerId/setActivePlayerId, executeCompetitiveDayStart, endCompetitiveMarketTurn, resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases, executeCompetitiveDay, checkCompetitiveEndConditions, updateCompetitiveScores. Serialization extended with activePlayerId/competitiveWinnerId. Tests: tests/main-street/competitive-phase.test.ts (28 tests) — alternation N=2/3/4, shared closing, thresholds, N=1 regression, invariants. Build green, unit suite 327 files / 5966 tests.
